problem: The figure puts the label R on the line joining the centres of two touching cells (A to B). Section 1 defines R as the distance from a cell centre to a hexagon corner, so the centre-to-centre distance between two touching cells is √3·R ≈ 1.73R, not R. A student will conclude that the cell radius equals the spacing between neighbouring base stations, which contradicts D = R√(3N) used just above.
fix: Remove the 'R' label from edge A–B, or relabel it '√3 R' and state in the caption that adjacent cell centres are √3 R apart when R is the centre-to-corner cell radius.

problem: The question asks to 'compare', but the answer only describes the two schemes. It gives no point of comparison, so a student writing only this would lose marks.
fix: Add the comparison: fixed is simple, needs no central coordination, but blocks calls under uneven load; dynamic uses the whole pool, serves hot spots better, but needs fast coordination and signalling to keep co-channel separation, so it costs more to run.
